items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Human Rights Forum (HRF) has condemned the Visakhapatnam police for preventing citizens from peacefully campaigning against the establishment of massive data centres in the city. On Sunday, August 9, which marked the anniversary of the Quit India movement, members of a group called Green Visakha had called for a procession on the Vizag beach road to spread awareness on the potential environmental impact of hyperscale artificial intelligence (AI) data centres. While police had earlier denied permission for the event, around 25 people gathered at the Bhagat Singh statue, and police arrived and objected to the small gathering too, HRF said. The Andhra Pradesh government has announced that it has entered agreements with various companies to establish data centres with a capacity of around nine gigawatts near Vizag. “The campaign aimed to confront serious questions arising from the sheer scale and concentration of these projects. items.title: The NEET aspirant who took the reservation debate to Jantar Mantar
items.summary: During the paper leak protests at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, NEET aspirant Harsh Dubey began appearing across media platforms to speak about reservation and challenge the Cockroach Janta Party’s approach. He soon became a talking point on social media, with pages such as ‘Aarakshan Hatao Andolan’ emerging in his support. In an interview with Newslaundry , Dubey says he is not opposed to reservation but wants reforms in the system. He says he plans to protest at Jantar Mantar from August 21 and wants people supporting him on social media to back his campaign the same way they supported the Cockroach Janta Party. Dubey also claims that the CJP protests were not representative of NEET aspirants. His basis for this? He says he spoke to 15-20 people at the protest and did not find a single NEET student among them. So what does Dubey’s call for reservation reform actually entail? Watch. In times of misinformation, you need news you can trust. We’ve got you covered. Subscribe to Newslaundry and power our work.

items.title: May collapse any moment: Rajasthan HC initiates suo motu PIL over unsafe dome of its own building
items.summary: The Rajasthan High Court on Monday initiated suo motu proceedings over the structural safety of its Jodhpur building. A Division Bench of Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Praveer Bhatnagar noted that its 21-metre-high central dome was at risk of imminent collapse, based on an assessment by the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Bombay. The Court observed that the dome was an ever-present threat posing a grave threat to human life. "This Court is gravely concerned with a matter of public importance and institutional significance, namely the structural condition of the building of the Rajasthan High Court, principal seat, including the central dome (approx. at a height of 21 metres) built and existing therein, which, according to the expert opinion of the Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay, is in a state of imminent collapse and may fall at any moment, thereby exposing the precious lives of all the stakeholders within the premises to grave and irreversible danger and damage," noted the Court. items.title: Allahabad HC orders ₹25 lakh compensation to 2 sisters illegally confined by family after conversion to Islam
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has ordered compensation of ₹25 lakh for 2 women who were illegally confined by their father after they converted from Hinduism to Islam. Justice Sandeep Jain ordered the women's father and the State government to jointly pay the amount after it found that they were forcibly confined in their parental home against their expressed wishes. In the judgment passed on August 6, the Court said that the sisters were deprived of their liberty for a prolonged period since 2021 and that the State, instead of securing their release, permitted the continuation of their illegal detention under the ostensible cover of criminal proceedings. "The record unmistakably reveals that the State machinery failed to discharge its constitutional obligations and, by its acts of omission and commission, lent tacit support to the continued deprivation of the fundamental rights of the corpus. Such executive inaction and constitutional indifference cannot receive judicial approbation and renders the State equally accountable in public law for the violation of the fundamental rights guaranteed to the corpus," the Court said. Archana Kalpathi was the producer of Chief Minister Vijay-starrer films Bigil (2019) and The Greatest of All Time (GOAT) (2024), both produced under AGS Entertainment. The seven-member committee has been constituted for a two-year term with effect from July 24, 2026. Archana Kalpathi is one of the five members of the committee. The other members are retired IAS officer P R Sampath, Ma Sumathi alias Sumathisri and Dr Tha Velmurugan. items.summary: As three fishermen who went missing at sea on July 31 remain untraceable, Kerala Chief Minister VD Satheesan announced that they would release a standard operating procedure (SOP) shortly for the safety of the coastal community. The CM was responding to protests about state apathy by the coastal community. Delegations led by the CM and other ministers on Monday, August 10, visited the houses of fishermen who went missing during accidents in Vizhinjam, Muthalapozhi and Neendakara. VD Satheesan and Minister of Forests Shibu Baby John visited the house of 26-year-old Gautam Krishna, who was among the 11 fishermen on board the boat ‘Miomi’ when it capsized near Neendakara on July 31. Gautam’s father, Radhakrishnan, 48, and grandfather, Rajeevan, 76, were killed in the accident, while the search for Gautam has entered Day 11. items.title: Hindutva ideologue TG Mohandas receives bail from Kerala court
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Nearly 24 hours after the arrest of Hindutva ideologue TG Mohandas, the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court in Thiruvananthapuram granted him bail on Monday, August 10. The Thiruvananthapuram Cyber Police arrested him on Sunday, August 9, over his derogatory and violent comments about student protesters at Jantar Mantar who were protesting over the NEET paper leak. According to reports , in his bail plea, Mohandas argued that he was exercising his right to freedom of expression and alleged that the case was politically motivated. He was granted bail on the condition that he cooperate with the investigation and not repeat the alleged offence. TG Mohandas, a former head of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Intellectual Cell in Kerala and a political commentator, had published multiple videos about the student protests on his YouTube channel, Pathrika. In two of the videos, he said the protesters at Jantar Mantar would have been shot and killed if he were in control. items.title: Jharkhand: Why are govt job aspirants protesting and what are their demands?
items.summary: Hundreds of government-job aspirants have been protesting in Ranchi for over two weeks, demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC). The protest began over allegations surrounding the 14th JPSC Combined Civil Services examination, but has since expanded into a larger movement demanding transparency and reform in the state’s recruitment system. The Jharkhand government has now agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC preliminary examination and two backlog examinations. Three JPSC members have also resigned. But students say they will not call off the agitation until their demand for a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the alleged irregularities, particularly the Jharkhand General Graduate Level Combined Competitive examination, commonly known as JSSC-CGL, is accepted. On Monday, August 10, students began marching towards the Jharkhand Assembly as part of a ‘Vidhan Sabha Gherao’.
